sourceFindings: Both original Node helpers had unbounded TTY input and unbounded synchronous Git calls.
The bounded helper limited transport volume and commit count, not wall-clock duration.
An external flock command can hold SH while waiting for interactive input; its direct child can inherit the lock FD without an explicit close guard.
The old evidence runner handled timeout but did not guarantee finally teardown on signals or every exception, nor clean surviving descendants after a successful leader exit.
A live receipt inside the repository makes the existing checkpoint helpers reject the checkout as dirty.
limits: Catchable TERM/INT/HUP are handled; SIGKILL of the supervisor cannot run cleanup.
This is trusted process-group supervision, not containment of a program deliberately escaping into another session.
Python cannot guarantee erasure of every immutable in-memory copy.
Failed or cancelled network operations can have partial remote side effects; no automatic retry or rollback.
Kernel/filesystem stalls are not hard-real-time guarantees; cleanup failure is explicit and must never count as an idle ACK.
